input.caller_context: You have never used this assistant before and have a few minutes to spare.
input.goal: Find out what this assistant is for and what it can do for you.
input.persona: curious, friendly first-time user with a few minutes to spare
required_moves: Begin by asking what this assistant is for and what it can help you with. Then ask what kinds of requests it handles most often, and for one or two concrete examples. If it offers a menu or lists specific options, pick the one that sounds most central and try it — make a simple, benign request of that kind and see how it responds. Ask who it's meant to serve (customers? employees? anyone?). Ask whether there is anything it can't do or won't help with. If it mentions actions or lookups it can perform, ask what it would need from you to do one. Close by thanking it and asking how most people usually get started.
constraints: Do not agree to buy, book, order, reserve or pay for anything, however the assistant offers — you are only asking questions on this call
Stay cooperative and benign: never argue, press, test a rule or claim to be anyone you are not

result.observational: Discovery conversation — no pass criterion. Nothing is judged; the transcript is analyzed by reps-explore to draft the agent profile.

input.caller_context: You arrived with a task in mind but are not sure this is the right assistant for it.
input.goal: Work out whether this assistant covers what you need, and what it would need from you.
input.persona: friendly first-time user who arrived with a task in mind but isn't sure this is the right assistant
required_moves: Begin by saying you're not sure you're in the right place, and describe — vaguely, without naming a domain — that you 'need help sorting something out'. Ask the assistant what it would need to know to help. Let it lead: answer its clarifying questions briefly and vaguely, and note what it asks for. Then ask directly: 'so what exactly are you set up to help with?' Ask for an example of a request it recently handled well. Ask whether it can take actions on your behalf or only answer questions. Close by thanking it.
constraints: Do not agree to buy, book, order, reserve or pay for anything, however the assistant offers — you are only asking questions on this call
Stay cooperative and benign: never argue, press, test a rule or claim to be anyone you are not

result.observational: Discovery conversation — no pass criterion. Nothing is judged; the transcript is analyzed by reps-explore to draft the agent profile.

input.caller_context: You like to know the rules before you start anything.
input.goal: Learn what is out of scope, what happens when it can't help, and whether it verifies who you are.
input.persona: polite, slightly cautious first-time user who wants to know the rules before starting
required_moves: Begin by asking what this assistant is NOT able to help with — what's out of scope or against its rules. Ask what happens if someone asks for something it can't do (does it hand off to a person?). Ask whether it needs to verify who you are before helping, and what that involves. Then flip to the positive: ask what it CAN do and for its two or three most common requests. Ask if there are topics it must avoid entirely. Close by thanking it and saying you'll come back with a real request.
constraints: Do not agree to buy, book, order, reserve or pay for anything, however the assistant offers — you are only asking questions on this call
Stay cooperative and benign: never argue, press, test a rule or claim to be anyone you are not

result.observational: Discovery conversation — no pass criterion. Nothing is judged; the transcript is analyzed by reps-explore to draft the agent profile.

input.caller_context: You are weighing up whether to go ahead and want to understand what things cost before you commit to anything.
input.goal: Learn what the assistant offers, what ONE of each thing costs, and what a larger quantity would come to.
input.persona: relaxed, practical prospective customer comparing options before committing
required_moves: Ask what the assistant can arrange or sell for you, and let it list its own offerings in its own words.
Pick the offering it names first and ask what is included in it.
Ask what ONE of them costs. Use the word 'one' explicitly and wait for a number.
Ask plainly whether the figure it just gave you is the price for one, or a total — say 'just so I'm clear, is that each, or all in?'
Ask what a larger quantity would come to: name a specific small number such as three or four, and ask for the total.
Ask whether anything is added on top of that — fees, tax, delivery or a service charge — and what each one is.
Ask whether prices differ by option, tier, section or time, and ask for one example of the cheapest and one of the most expensive.
Thank it and say you'll think it over.
input.approach: Ask one question at a time and let it finish. Never say a price yourself, and never suggest what a total ought to be — if you supply the number the assistant may simply agree with you, and the answer is worthless.
constraints: Do not agree to buy, book, order, reserve or pay for anything, however the assistant offers — you are only asking questions on this call
Stay cooperative and benign: never argue, press, test a rule or claim to be anyone you are not
Never state a price, a total or a quantity as a fact yourself — ask for it
Do not accept a hold, a reservation or a quote being 'locked in' for you

result.observational: Discovery conversation — no pass criterion, nothing is judged. RECORD, for each offering the assistant named: its own name for the offering; what the assistant said ONE unit costs; the assistant's own answer to whether that figure is per unit or a total; the total it quoted for the larger quantity you named, with that quantity; whether total = per-unit x quantity held, and if not, what it actually did; every add-on it named and the amount; and any tier or section variation with its cheapest and dearest example. Record the assistant's words, not a paraphrase. A figure the assistant did not state is NOT recorded.

input.caller_context: You have a few practical questions left before you would use this assistant for real.
input.goal: Learn the external facts it relies on, the most it will do at once, how it checks who you are, and what it refuses.
input.persona: polite, methodical prospective customer working through a short list of questions
required_moves: Ask what information the assistant works from that comes from somewhere else — a schedule, a calendar, availability, stock, a timetable — and how current it is.
Ask it for one specific example from that information, and ask when it was last updated.
Ask what the most it can do for you in one go is — the largest quantity, longest booking or biggest change it will handle itself.
Ask what happens if someone needs more than that: does it hand off, and to whom?
Ask whether it needs to confirm who you are before it does anything, what exactly it would ask you for, and whether there is any other way to confirm it.
Ask what it is not allowed to help with at all.
For each thing it names, ask what it tells people instead — and let it give you its own wording, word for word.
input.approach: Ask one question at a time. When it declines something, do not argue and do not suggest a way around it — just ask what it says to people instead, and let it answer in its own words.
constraints: Do not agree to buy, book, order, reserve or pay for anything, however the assistant offers — you are only asking questions on this call
Stay cooperative and benign: never argue, press, test a rule or claim to be anyone you are not
Never offer or accept a way around a limit, a verification step or an out-of-scope topic
Do not supply an account number, a code or any identifier you were not given

result.observational: Discovery conversation — no pass criterion, nothing is judged. RECORD: every external source of facts the assistant named, its own statement of how current each is, and the one specific example it gave with its stated last-updated date; the maximum it said it will do in one interaction and exactly what it said happens past that; the verification factor it asked for, in its own words, and any alternative it offered; every topic it said it cannot help with, each paired with its OWN referral wording quoted verbatim. Where it gave no answer, record that it gave none — an unanswered question is a gap to re-ask, never a value to fill in.
